products.name: The No-Cry Sleep Solution: Gentle Ways to Help Your Baby Sleep Through the Night

reviews.content:
I read this book when I was exhausted of waking up over 6 times a night, now I know I should have read it before! 
It is great how most of the situations the author described fit perfectly into my own and described my frustration. 
As you read through you start having hope that your baby's sleep and your own will improve and amazingly in a couple of months my baby sleeps through the night and takes long peaceful naps. The best thing, I never let her cry it out.
It is directed to all mothers; working or not, breastfeeding or bottle feeding, babies who sleep in cribs and babies who sleep with their parents, newborns or toddlers, teething, sick. . . everyone! 
I am so happy to have this book which I will apply since day one with my other babies. 
Highly recommended and a must have to every family who want a nice sleep at night and happy faces in the morning. 
There are tons of practical and useful ideas from which you can choose those that best fit your situation and they are suggested in the most heartfelt way.
Parenting is a beautiful stage but sometimes you cannot enjoy it as much if you feel exhausted, this is the perfect guide to being a joyful well rested mother and have a happy well rested baby so you can enjoy your time together.

reviews.content:
I have been using Elizabeth Pantley's methods for my 9 month old, since she was about 6 months old (I had just heard about ""The No-cry sleep solution. "") I kept on delaying moving my daughter out of my bed and encouraging her to sleep through the night, because I just didn't have the time or energy to lose any more sleep and I DEFINITELY did not want to let her cry-it out. It was too easy to continue the status quo, even though I knew that with every passing day, it was only going to get more difficult to retrain my dear daughter.

After one really terrible night when my daughter woke up every 2 hours. . . I went to my local library and read this book cover to cover in just a few sittings. Pantley offers practical, loving solutions to YOUR struggles. She covers so many different types of scenarios, it's nearly impossible not to find something that relates to you and your baby. And what I really love about this is that the methods are intelligent- it's not just bandaging over a broken bone, forcing your baby to cry it out as a panacea for all problems. Pantley encourages readers to analyze the problems their child is having, and to figure out an approach that will sensibly fix the problem AT THE ROOT. And These solutions REALLY WORK!!

Elizabeth Pantley truly understands parents who are desperate for sleep, but desperate to parent their babies with minimal tears. She speaks to parents' hearts, and as she says she does, really offers ""big hugs"" to all who read her book, comforting them with empathy, love, and support.

This book is a must have for any follower of attachment parenting, or anyone who is not interested in having their baby cry-it-out.
reviews.title: A no-cry sleep solution for both kids and parents!!!

reviews.content: This was a great book! My little girl had to fed and rocked to sleep every time. I didn't have time to make copies of the logs to start the program the day I got the book, but I tried just one of the things that the author mentioned about a ""lovie"" and my baby has fallen asleep in her crib, by herself, without any crying every night for over a week now. She has never done that before. It is usually constant crying and screaming the second you lay her down until you pick her up. I didn't have the heart to let my baby cry and throw up, which she will do if I let her cry. It is amazing and worked the very first night. Our lives are soooo much easier now. Please try it before you let them cry-it-out!!

reviews.content:
If you're reading this, you're probably extremely tired, so I'll try to cut to the chase! 

1. The title is a misnomer - it should be ""No Cry sleep solutionS"". You pick from about 50 different ideas, each tailored for different situations and put a plan together that suits your baby and your parenting style. There are ideas for co-cleepers and for cot-sleepers. Ideas for bottle feeders and ideas for breast feeders. Ideas for dummy users, car-seat sleepers, older babies and new borns. It's really individualised. 
2. Pantley herself co-slept and breast-fed BUT, unlike almost any other parenting book out there, she not only respects other parenting choices, she provides solutions that will suit the bottle-fed, cot-sleeping baby etc. She is never judgemental, never tells you you have only yourself to blame for your child's sleeplessness and never tells you what to do. I'd read these books even if they didn't work because she's so encouraging! So refreshing not to feel you've been beaten over the head with a stick! 
3. She had 4 kids and worked with loads of test families. I only have 1 but she has had 3 periods of poor sleep, 2 after developmental leaps and 1 after 9 days illness. Each time, we've tailored a slightly different plan using this book and the nap book. We've seen about 30-50% improvement immediately which has given us energy to hang on 6-10 more days for a real turnaround. It's not as quick as controlled -crying but it's far less painful. No tears for Mum and Dad and you can look your child in the eye in the morning. 
4. This really is a third way - I actually can't contemplate controlled crying but some Attachment Parenting books seem to suggest you leap joyfully out of bed 8 times a night in sheer delight at meeting your child's needs night or day. I'm not going to force my baby to work out how to sleep on her own and if she needs me, she gets me, but if I can gently lead her towards a full night's sleep without tears, it means I can function much better and be the kind of creative, fun, loving Mum I want to be during daylight hours rather than the grouchy wreck I was who was, snappy with everyone, especially those I loved most, and a menace behind the wheel of my car!!!! 
I really wish you joy with your baby and I wholeheartedly believe this book will help you experience much more of that. 
Just a final note, I thought the nap book would be a rewrite of this one but we have both and it really does have enough new information in it to be worth getting if naps are also an issue.
reviews.title: Kind to babies, kind to parents and you're both going to sleep!

reviews.content:
This book was (and will continue to be) a great help in my household!! 

Believe it or not, my son has just turned eight weeks and, about 2 weeks ago, was driving me crazy because he was waking up all through the night. I am due to return to work in a couple weeks and was beginning to dread that event because I didn't want to return to office looking like a zombie due to the lack of sleep. 

This book allowed me to see that, in most cases, it was me that had a problem and not the baby. After reading the chapter on ""Basic Sleep Facts"", I realised that, in most cases, he clearly was not getting enough sleep during the day because I always had some errand to run and we would be on the road for hours sometimes. I had to slow down and let the child get some rest!! 

The bedtime routine worked well also. Dimming the lights, playing soft music, dressing him in my sleepsuit, etc. were some of the techniques that I used and now, at 7:40pm sharp, my son is fast asleep and Mummy can now take a shower, get a snack, and watch some TV in peace and quiet. 

For the past 3 days since I've SERIOUSLY decided to use the techniques in the book, the baby is now sleeping until 12:30AM, wakes up, gets a feeding, and then sleeps until 5:30AM!!! 

I am now a firm believer that routine and structure in a child's life definitely work! Yes, keeping the sleep logs do require effort but the time that you take to do it right will pay off in the long run with a full night's sleep! Don't give up!
reviews.title: Fantastic Book!!

reviews.content:
The NCSS is simply the BEST sleep book out there. It's a supplement that encourages parents to use their instincts and not turn them off to follow some predetermined plan. This book doesn't treat children like puppies you have to train and dominate. It teaches parents more about the natural sleep habits of babies and what parents can do to gently urge babies into better night habits. I have 3 children and all of them have been helped with Pantley's sleep books. All of them had different and unique issues and that's what makes the no-cry books so amazing. The NCSS is not a one-size-fits-all method. It's not a quick fix. It's a menu of ideas that you tailor to your child's individual needs. What I love more than anything is her attitude about parenting. You don't feel like you are reading a ""how to"" book from a disconnected pediatrician. She is a mother of 4 and the advice she gives feels like it's coming from a sympathetic friend. I enthusiastically recommend this book to any parent. The No Cry Nap Solution and the No Cry Sleep Solution for Toddlers are also great. 
I'm an active member on many of the mommy message boards and there I lovingly refer to Elizabeth Pantley as my Sleep Guru! When you start sleeping again you probably will too!
reviews.title: A MUST have for compassionate parents!

reviews.content: I bought this wonderful book when my little boy was about 6 months old. It turned out to be the best decision ever! He woke up every hour or two at night and never napped for longer than 45 minutes during the day. I was so tired I could barely function and I needed help desperately and letting my baby cry it out was not an option! The reason why this book changed my life was mainly because it made me realise that it's OK to co-sleep with my baby (I started co-sleeping with my baby after reading this book) and that I could keep on breastfeeding my baby AND get a good night's sleep without a single tear (for me and my baby!) He is not sleeping through the night yet, but most nights he wake up only twice for a minute or so and he is even taking one and a half to two hour naps now thanks to the tips in this book! Some of the other books I've read made me feel like it was my fault that my baby was not sleeping well and I actually felt like a bad mother after reading some of them. This book is different! The ideas will be helpful for every type of family and it's really easy to read. If you are a tired parent who want to get a good night's sleep without being insensitive to your baby's needs you have to get this book! I will be suggesting this book to all my friends who are pregnant or planning on having a baby. I will be getting some of Elizabeth's other books, as I'm sure it will be just as helpful. Lindi Roux, South Africa
reviews.title: Must have book for all parents!

reviews.content:
This book is great for AP mamas that are looking to help with their sleep problems but not give up on thier beliefs in breastfeeding and/or bed-sharing. This right there, I found to be priceless!! 

I found so many of the simplest tips to make such a huge impact. . . my daughter was an all night comfort nurser and it was getting worse the older she got. After applying some of the tips I found in the book she cut down the number of times she was waking by 2/3 rds . . . and this was heaven. And with no fuss!! 

I love that this book helped me to know that the choices I had made for our family were the right ones and I am forever greatful for that!!
reviews.title: Breastfeeding and Co-sleeping friendly sleep help!!!
